parent_protocol.analysis_report_sha_note: runs/holdout_analysis_v1/analysis.json is unchanged by this amendment

purpose: Post-confirmatory, descriptive analyses on the same 500 holdout participants: (A) a second unsupervised domain-adaptation baseline (AdaBN) and (B) a test-time input-amplitude sweep probing whether N3 under-detection depends on signal amplitude. Neither analysis changes or re-tests H1-H3.
status_of_holdout: Holdout labels were used once by the parent analysis. The model (E4 seed 42) was chosen after that analysis because the manuscript recommends the band-pass-only form of the pipeline, of which E3 and E4 are equivalent runs (post-hoc checkpoint comparison, runs/e3_e4_checkpoint_comparison). No scale factor, threshold or adaptation setting depends on holdout results; every condition below is fixed before any amendment inference.

model.checkpoints: the gate-verified E4 seed-42 checkpoints of the parent run (runs/holdout_ckpt_restore_20261010)
model.ensembling: arithmetic mean of the ten fold softmax probabilities (float64 accumulator, float32 storage), argmax

reference_condition.name: E4_s42
reference_condition.source: existing parent ensembles in runs/holdout_inference_v1/ensemble/E4_s42 (equivalent to input scale 1.0)
reference_condition.reproduction_check: before inference, the amendment code path must reproduce the stored parent fold probabilities of E4_s42 for two records at folds 0 and 9 (max |difference| <= 1e-5, identical argmax)

input_scale: every sample of every bandpass_v2 epoch is multiplied by the factor before the encoder; the encoder runs in evaluation mode with its stored batch-normalisation statistics; the TCN is unchanged

adabn.reference: Li et al., Revisiting batch normalization for practical domain adaptation (AdaBN)
adabn.layers: all ten BatchNorm1d layers of the ResNet-1D encoder; affine parameters unchanged; the TCN (LayerNorm only) is unchanged

sample.selection: uniform without replacement over all epochs stored for each record (the evaluation window), using numpy default_rng([2041, int(subject_id)]); labels are not read

adabn.estimation: layer by layer in forward-execution order; each layer's running mean and running variance are replaced by the per-channel mean and population variance of its input over all positions of the 20,000 sampled epochs, computed after all earlier layers have been adapted; one adapted encoder per fold
adabn.transductive_scope: cohort level (statistics pooled over the 500 holdout recordings)

amplitude_descriptive.statistic: per-record standard deviation (population) of the bandpass_v2 input over all stored epochs, in microvolts; labels not read
amplitude_descriptive.summary: median and interquartile range per cohort, and the ratio of the SHHS1 median to the Sleep-EDF median

statistics.metric_definitions: as in the parent protocol: subject-mean macro-F1 over five fixed classes with F1 = 0 for absent classes; pooled metrics from summed confusion matrices

contrasts_vs_E4_s42: pooled N1, N2, N3 and REM F1
contrasts_adabn: adabn - ADAST_full_e30: subject-mean macro-F1 and pooled N3 recall

pre_specified_expectation: If N3 under-detection arises mainly because SHHS1 slow waves reach the encoder at a smaller amplitude than the Sleep-EDF training data, N3 recall should increase and the N3-to-N2 rate decrease with factors above 1, and change in the opposite direction with factors below 1. A flat or non-monotonic response is evidence against an amplitude-only explanation.
interpretation_rules: All results are descriptive and post-confirmatory; they do not alter the H1-H3 decisions.
No scale factor is selected, recommended or reported as an improved pipeline.
AdaBN is reported as a label-free domain-adaptation baseline; a difference is described as a gain or loss only when its 95% interval excludes zero.
Results are reported in full regardless of direction.
prohibited: adding, removing or changing conditions after amendment inference has started
reading reference labels before all amendment ensembles exist
using any amendment result to choose a model for the confirmatory claims
